about.title: Concord Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A faulty product doesn't announce itself. In Concord, it might be a space heater that overheats in a home off Clayton Road, a child's car seat that fails on SR-4, or a power tool that shatters mid-job. When something you bought and used as intended causes harm, California law tends to look at the product, not your behavior. Under strict liability, you generally need to show the item was defective in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. Proving the manufacturer was careless is usually not required. That distinction matters for Contra Costa County families who simply want to be made whole. Everyone in the chain of sale can share responsibility here: the company that built the product, the distributor that shipped it, and the Concord retailer that sold it. We handle product liability cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My car's airbag didn't deploy in a crash on SR-242. Is that a product liability case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Concord recorded 481 injury collisions in 2025, and when a safety component fails during one of them, a separate claim against the vehicle or part manufacturer may exist alongside any claim against another driver. We can review the vehicle and the crash details to see whether a defect played a role. Try not to have the car repaired or scrapped before that review.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was flawed?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability often runs on strict liability, meaning you typically need to show the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that it caused your injury. The manufacturer's knowledge or carefulness is usually not the deciding issue. That said, every case turns on its own facts, which is why speaking with us matters.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront?
items.answer: No. We handle product liability cases on contingency, so you owe no attorney fee unless there is a recovery. You are free to decide whether to move forward after your first consultation with us.
